questions.q: Explain why an operating system gives each user their own account.

markPoints.concept: each user has their own files and settings
accept: own files|own documents|own settings|own desktop|separate files|their files|personal
markPoints.exemplar: Each user has their own files and settings.

markPoints.concept: and the system can control what each one is allowed to do
markPoints.exemplar: The system can also control what each one is allowed to do.

questions.example: Each user gets their own files, settings and desktop, which stay private from the others, and the operating system can control what each account is allowed to see and change.
questions.paraphrase: Everyone has their own documents and preferences kept apart from other people's, and the system decides what each person has permission to do.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.5 Lesson 3 — Accounts office, station 1: User accounts

questions.q: Which of these are jobs an operating system does when it manages files? Tick all that apply.
options: Keeping track of where each file is stored
Letting the user rename, move and delete files
Controlling which users can open which files
Deciding what a file's contents mean
Choosing which program the user should write next
correct: Keeping track of where each file is stored
Letting the user rename, move and delete files
Controlling which users can open which files
questions.feedback: The operating system looks after where files are and who may touch them. What is inside them is the application's business.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.5 Lesson 3 — Accounts office, station 1: User accounts

questions.q: Match each account to the access it should be given on a school network.
pairs: Read and write their own files, read shared resources
Read and write their class's work and enter marks
Install software and change settings on any machine
Reach the internet and nothing else
questions.feedback: Each account gets what the job needs and no more. That principle is what limits the damage when an account is misused.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.5 Lesson 3 — Accounts office, station 2: Access levels

questions.q: Explain why a school does not give every pupil the same access rights as a technician.

markPoints.concept: a technician's account can change settings and install software
accept: install|change settings|change anything|alter|delete|admin|administrator|full access|everything|any machine|system files|system itself
markPoints.exemplar: A technician's account can install software.

markPoints.concept: so if a pupil's account were misused or stolen the damage would be far worse
markPoints.exemplar: This means a misused pupil account could damage the whole network rather than just their own files.

questions.example: A technician's account can install software and change system settings on any machine. If every pupil had that, one careless mistake or one stolen password could break machines for everybody rather than affecting only that pupil's own files.
questions.paraphrase: Because such an account can alter the system itself, giving it to everyone would mean a single error or compromised login could affect the entire network.
questions.feedback: What the extra rights allow, and what goes wrong when they are misused.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.5 Lesson 3 — Accounts office, station 2: Access levels

questions.q: What does a file's extension tell the operating system?
options: Which program should be used to open it
Where on the disk the file is stored
Who is allowed to open it
questions.feedback: The extension is how the operating system knows which program a file belongs to. Size, location and permissions are all recorded separately.
questions.subtopic: File extensions and what the OS does with files

questions.q: Which of these does an operating system do when it manages files? Tick all that apply.
options: Records where on the disk each file is stored
Keeps a folder structure so files can be organised
Records which account owns each file
Opens a file in the right program when it is double-clicked
Decides whether the contents of a file are correct
Writes the contents of the file for the user
correct: Records where on the disk each file is stored
Keeps a folder structure so files can be organised
Records which account owns each file
Opens a file in the right program when it is double-clicked
questions.feedback: Where it is, who owns it, how it is organised and what opens it. What is inside it is the application's business.
